answer: A farm that wants 211 keys as a result burns 211 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the wharf seed, the mirror timing is verifiable from the quill record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 547 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
